name: Isle of Dread
summary: South of Sardor Isle, sheer cliffs guard the Isle of Dread off Feralas’s southwestern coast. Chimaeroks roam its highlands, while naga hide in sea caves.

sections.title: A Land of Monsters and Tides
sections.body: A narrow path on the southeastern shore leads you into the island’s high valley. Two-headed chimaeroks roam this enclosed highland, strengthened by arcane energies. Lord Lakmaeran leads the beasts. Anyone crossing from Sardor Isle faces danger here.

sections.title: The Northern Caverns
sections.body: Hatecrest naga occupy caves along the island’s northern shore. Lord Shalzaru leads them as they plot against the night elven sentinels at nearby Feathermoon Stronghold. Submerged passages wind through the deep chambers to secluded grottoes. Their fortified lair stays beyond mainland scrutiny.

faq.q: How do you reach the interior of the Isle of Dread?
aliases: how to get up isle of dread
faq.answer: Sheer cliffs block the way up from nearly every shore. A natural path on the southeastern side leads on foot to the central plateau.

faq.q: What kinds of creatures inhabit the island?
faq.answer: Fierce chimaeroks roam the high plateau, including arcane chimaeroks and massive devourers led by Lord Lakmaeran. Hostile Hatecrest naga occupy deep sea caves along the northern coast.

faq.q: Who leads the naga in the sea caves?
faq.answer: Lord Shalzaru leads the naga in the northern caves. Their presence threatens the nearby night elves at Feathermoon Stronghold.

faq.q: What makes chimaerok meat so famous?
faq.answer: Chimaeroks yield rich, tender meat prized by master gourmands. Dirge Quikcleave seeks meat from the island, including Lord Lakmaeran’s carcass, to craft legendary feasts.

angles.text: The Isle of Dread’s chimaeroks are the only known source of Chimaerok Tenderloin, the key ingredient in Dirge Quikcleave’s legendary Chimaerok Chops.
Night elven sentinels at nearby Feathermoon Stronghold watch the isle. They seek brave champions to strike at Lord Shalzaru and halt the naga presence off their shores.
